newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia sultan defies Mahathir on new minister.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia sultan defies Mahathir on new minister.

text.p: A Malaysian sultan said on Monday he had rejected Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's choice of a new chief minister for his state after the man who held the post resigned over a scandal, the Bernama news agency reported.

"I do not agree to all the names submitted to me. Therefore, Dr Mahathir said it will have to be postponed until I can give my consent," Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah of central Selangor state was quoted as telling a news conference.
The previous chief minister, Muhammad Muhammad Taib, quit his post this month after being charged in an Australian court with bringing in nearly $1 million in undeclared cash into Australia.
Bernama said Mahathir was expected to name a replacement for Muhammad after an audience with the sultan. But Mahathir left the meeting without comment, it said.
"Experience is not needed, honesty is," the sultan told reporters when asked to comment on what he expected of the new chief minister. Selangor had leaders "but they're unsuitable", he added.
Abdul Aziz said Mahathir was expected to submit a new list of candidates for his approval within two weeks.
Malaysia's sultans have rarely turned down proposals by the prime minister, especially since Mahathir moved to clip their powers, which included immunity from prosecution, in 1994.

Malaysia's nine sultans play a symbolic role as protectors of the politically dominant ethnic Malays and keepers of Islam. Under Malaysia's rotating monarchy, they take turns every five years at being king.
Abdul Aziz defied Mahathir once before in 1990 by initially hesitating to reappoint Muhammad after he had eloped with the sultan's daughter.
